c01-1: The four heads of 1868 made their marks on the same document.
c01-2: Useful document: the extract from the cadastral roll and its transfers, at the cadastre.
c01-3: Lot 1, “Goémard Gervais”, amber gatherer: the Fork alone, the foot plain, the full mark of a head of 1868.
c02-1: A wife keeps her husband's mark, with a heel: a small head of the house she was born into.
c02-2: Useful document: the marriage of a Goémard son, in 1879.
c02-3: At the foot of the entry, without captions, the parents mark in the order in which they come up. “Perrine Oyard, spinner”: the Fork, a small Eye at the heel.
c03-1: The four heads of 1868 made their marks on the same document.
c03-2: Useful document: the extract from the cadastral roll and its transfers, at the cadastre.
c03-3: Lot 2, “Oyard Clovis”, gulf pilot: the Eye alone, the foot plain.
c04-1: She was a midwife, like another woman in the tree: do not confuse them.
c04-2: Useful document: the 1876 marriage, at Port-Sénane.
c04-3: “The marks of the fathers and mothers, made one after the other”: the Eye, a small Arrow at the heel.
c05-1: The four heads of 1868 made their marks on the same document.
c05-2: Useful document: the extract from the cadastral roll and its transfers, at the cadastre.
c05-3: Lot 3, “Cormaud Siméon”, shipwright: the Arrow alone, the foot plain.
c06-1: An object saved from the island bears her mark; her trade was nets.
c06-2: Useful document: the photograph of the boatshed (1964).
c06-3: The netting needle, on the bench: the Arrow, a small Gallows at the heel.
c07-1: The four heads of 1868 made their marks on the same document.
c07-2: Useful document: the extract from the cadastral roll and its transfers, at the cadastre.
c07-3: Lot 4, “Lestaud Lubin”, seaweed gatherer: the Gallows alone, the foot plain.
c08-1: She was known by her oven.
c08-2: Useful document: the marriage of her daughter Reine, in 1879.
c08-3: “Apolline Goémard, baker at the island's common oven”: the Gallows, a small Fork at the heel.
c09-1: He succeeded his father in the cadastre.
c09-2: Useful document: the transfers in the cadastral roll.
c09-3: “Goémard Josse succeeds Gervais” (1887): the Fork, a notch on the left, the eldest.
c10-1: Before she was a wife, she was a daughter: her mark changed.
c10-2: Useful document: her marriage to Josse, in 1879.
c10-3: One grain: Lubin's elder daughter. As a wife, she takes Josse's Fork with a small Gallows at the heel (the spindle in the shed).
c11-2: Useful document: the marriage of Lazare Cormaud and Victoire Oyard (1913).
c11-3: “Jacquette Goémard, midwife, his widow”: Médard's Eye, notch on the left, and a small Fork at the heel.
c12-1: His daughter talks about him on a 1964 tape.
c12-2: Useful documents: the tape “The marks”; the cadastre transfers.
c12-3: He “had the Eye and a notch on the left”: Clovis's eldest, a boatman; he succeeds his father in 1880.
c13-1: An 1854 baptism, in the copy of the chapel register.
c13-2: Useful documents: the first notebook of the Brémoy copy; the sealed letter of 1908.
c13-3: The younger one, “son of Gervais”. The Fork, notch on the right: the one on the fireplace, and the one on the “B.”.
c14-2: Useful documents: the 1878 marriage; the shopfront of the Ferlay bookshop.
c14-3: “Amélie Ferlay, bookseller”; in the photograph, half-moon spectacles and a book held against her chest.
c15-1: A mark copied by a clerk is not a mark.
c15-2: Useful document: the 1877 marriage, original and duplicate side by side.
c15-3: On the original, the Eye and a grain; the cross in the duplicate is the clerk's. As a wife: Fulbert's Gallows, a small Eye at the heel (the bread stamp).
c16-1: He succeeded his father in the cadastre.
c16-2: Useful document: the transfers in the cadastral roll.
c16-3: “Lestaud Fulbert succeeds Lubin” (1893): the Gallows, a notch on the left.
c17-1: Look on the Lights and Beacons side.
c17-2: Useful document: the staff register of the gulf lights.
c17-3: He was “appointed assistant keeper of the light”, not lighthouse keeper: read the definition at the head of the register. The Gallows, notch on the right.
c18-2: Useful document: the photograph of the school (1897).
c18-3: The names are on the back, in her hand: “In the middle, me”. The pince-nez on a black cord.
c19-3: Born “of parents unknown, taken in and brought up by Siméon Cormaud”: the Arrow, barred.
c20-3: “Honorine Lestaud, net mender”: Noël's barred Arrow, a small Gallows at the heel.
c21-1: His son is a fishing skipper at the Cabanes.
c21-2: Useful document: the ten-year indexes of the Cabanes section.
c21-3: “Gatien Goémard, amber cutter”; on the back of his wedding photograph, his name; the eyebrows raised to a point.
c22-2: Useful document: the ten-year indexes of the Cabanes section.
c22-3: “Léontine Sauvat, seamstress”, on the back of the 1911 photograph; the pincushion on her wrist.
c23-2: Useful document: the photograph of the boatshed (1964).
c23-3: His oar: the Eye, two notches on the left, the eldest of the eldest.
c25-2: Useful documents: the 1913 marriage; the wedding, in the Friendly Society's album.
c25-3: “Lazare Cormaud, fisherman”; his father's very curly black hair.
c26-2: Useful documents: the 1913 marriage; the photograph of the wedding.
c26-3: “Clément Lestaud, sailor”; the big, sticking-out ears of the Lestauds.
c27-2: Useful documents: the 1924 death; the photograph of the Cabanes workshop (1912).
c27-3: “Mr Léandre Garnaud, director”; the amber charm and the raised eyebrows.
c28-2: Useful document: the photograph of the jetty, in The Echo of 15 October 1977.
c28-3: Mr Félix Goémard, “skipper of the Saint-Gervais”; the scar on his chin.
c29-2: Useful document: the photograph of the stall (about 1935).
c29-3: “Mrs Pellerin, née Rose Oyard”; the very pale eyes of the Oyards.
c30-2: Useful document: the photograph of the boatshed (1964).
c30-3: Marin Cormaud, “president, foreman at the Cabanes workshop”; the curly hair of his grandfather Noël.
c31-1: A note on the island's birds.
c31-2: Useful document: the photograph of the tern ringing (1961).
c31-3: “A. L., Gulf Ornithological Society”; the sticking-out ears of the Lestauds.
c32-2: Useful document: the portrait in The Echo of 15 October 1977.
c32-3: Miss Edmée Garnaud, “president of the Amber Company”; the amber brooch with the insect.
g-matrice-1: The four heads made their marks on the same document.
g-matrice-2: Useful document: the extract from the 1868 roll.
g-matrice-3: They “made their mark”: the head alone, the foot plain.
g-oyard-1: One house, the Eye: the head of 1868, his descendants, and a wife who came from elsewhere.
g-oyard-3: One notch on the left for the eldest, two for the eldest of the eldest; a daughter signs with a grain.
g-talons-1: A wife keeps her husband's mark; look under the foot.
g-talons-2: Useful document: the grammar of the marks, plate I of the notebook.
g-talons-3: The heel: a small head of the house she was born into.
g-ecole-1: The school and the light: a schoolmistress, a keeper, and the keeper's sister.
g-ecole-2: Useful document: the letter from Mrs Sollier.
g-ecole-3: The Longuegrève light is not a lighthouse.
g-goemard-1: The Fork after 1868: the eldest, his wife, his son, his daughter-in-law, his grandson.
g-goemard-2: Useful document: the ten-year indexes of the Cabanes section.
g-goemard-3: Josse's son signs; his mark is only on an oar.
g-lestaud-1: The Gallows after 1868: the eldest, his wife, their son, their granddaughter.
g-lestaud-2: Useful document: the 1877 marriage, original and duplicate.
g-lestaud-3: A mark copied by a clerk does not count.
g-mer-1: A mark can bear the head of a house without being of its blood.
g-mer-2: Useful document: the grammar of the marks, plate I of the notebook.
g-mer-3: The sea child: “you bar its foot”.
g-garnaud-1: The head and the notches are enough to designate a single person.
g-garnaud-2: Useful document: the first notebook of the Brémoy copy.
g-garnaud-3: “Blaise, son of Gervais”: the younger son, notch on the right.
